title.en: How to connect an AI agent to TraderBuddy over MCP

description.en: Connect Claude Code, Cursor or any MCP client to TraderBuddy in three steps: a personal access token, one command, a check. What the agent can do, and what it never can.

children.text: TraderBuddy runs an MCP server, so Claude Code, Cursor and other AI agents can look up a stock, read your alerts and portfolios, and manage alerts, your watchlist, chart drawings, saved scanners, the daily digest and your portfolio transactions without opening the browser. It takes about two minutes to connect. It tracks and alerts; it never trades, and nothing an agent does can place an order.
Once it is connected, you talk to your agent in plain words and it calls TraderBuddy's tools for you:
"Give me the full picture on NVDA."
Price and 1d to 1y change, the 52-week range, distance from the 50- and 200-day averages, RSI, valuation, analyst ratings, and whether you already watch, hold or have an alert on it.
"Alert me if SPY closes below its 200-day average."
"Which of my alerts have triggered this month, and why?"
"Scan the S&P 500 for stocks with RSI under 30 that are still above their 200-day average, and save it as 'Dip buys'."
"Draw a support line at 187.50 on AAPL and alert me on it."
"What are the macro readings that say risk-off right now?"
, and it signs you in with a

that you create yourself. There is no OAuth sign-in for agents: Zitadel, the identity provider, does not support the dynamic client registration agents need, so a token is how an agent proves it is acting for you.

fields.source:
direction: right
agent: "AI agent\n(Claude Code, Cursor)"
tb: TraderBuddy API {
  mcp: "MCP server\n/api/mcp/"
  door: "Token check\nscope + allowlist"
  rest: "REST API\nsame as the browser"
  mcp -> door -> rest
}
agent -> tb.mcp: "tool call\nAuthorization: Bearer tb_pat_…"
fields.alt: An AI agent sends each MCP call with a bearer token to TraderBuddy; the MCP server calls the same REST API the browser uses, which checks the token's scope before any data is read or written

children.text: The MCP server is not a separate service. It lives inside the API, and every tool calls the same REST routes the browser uses, carrying your token. So an agent gets exactly what you get in the browser: the same validation, the same approval check, the same per-user privacy and the same rate limits. Nothing is reimplemented, so nothing can drift or be bypassed.
. Give it a name you will recognise ("Claude Code on laptop"), choose what it may do, and pick an expiry: 30 days, 90 days or a year. There is no "never".
Look at everything listed below. Change nothing.

What an agent can never do
These are not settings. They are walls in the API, enforced no matter which client or token is used:
There is no order entry anywhere in TraderBuddy.
It can see that a Slack, Telegram or webhook channel exists and whether it works, but cannot add, change, remove or test one. Otherwise bot tokens would end up in the agent's conversation history.
, even if your account is an admin. A token carries no roles.
Only a signed-in browser can, so a leaked read-only token cannot upgrade itself.
It can add and correct transactions, but not delete a transaction or a portfolio, rename one, or import a file. Anything it adds wrongly, you remove in the browser.
Anything not on the allowlist is refused by default, and a test fails the build if a new route is added without a decision about whether tokens may reach it.

They are checked once per trading day, after the US close. "Alert me when it crosses 200" means "tell me after the close on the day it did". The agent is told this and should not promise instant notification.
